main_topics.reason: The user opened asking which RA drugs are safe while trying and during pregnancy and kept returning to it across many turns.
The user disclosed being on methotrexate and asked whether to worry, then asked about the washout and contraception.
The user asked for a step-by-step sequence for trying in about 18 months and about a backup if the switch failed.
The user asked what happens if the new medication controls RA less well than methotrexate.
The user asked whether RA changes in pregnancy and learned about postpartum flares.
The user asked in one turn whether the pregnancy-safe medications are also fine with breastfeeding.
The user asked who to coordinate with and whether to raise pregnancy plans with the rheumatologist now.
The user raised it briefly as a new realisation and did not return to it.
The user said they came in anxious and framed the fear as a choice between health and a baby, and later felt relieved.

output.summary: A user recently diagnosed with rheumatoid arthritis wanted to plan medication choices ahead of trying for a baby in one to two years. They learned which medications are pregnancy-compatible, that they are currently on methotrexate and must plan a washout and contraception, and got a timeline, a note on postpartum flares and breastfeeding, and advice to raise it with their rheumatologist. The user ended confident and relieved, saying they felt they had a handle on it. No safety-critical moments occurred.
